call_points.text: Management plans to return 50% of cumulative adjusted free cash flow to shareholders over rolling five-year periods.
Technology and AI investments are being funded entirely from operating cash flows.
Group premiums grew 21.8% in H1FY27, significantly outperforming the industry growth of 15.3%.
Retention rates are expected to normalize within 3 to 4 quarters as the churn tail end from the Paramount acquisition runs its course.
International revenue pools are diversifying with retail and technology segments showing the fastest growth.
No numeric FY27 guidance; tech and international growth expected to continue at FY26 rates, core business to match or better industry.
call_points.versus_prior: reiterated: no numeric FY27 guidance, as in the Q4FY26 call

call_points.text: Over 50% of Paramount claims volume has moved to MAtrix; it should be the primary processing engine before Q2FY27.
call_points.versus_prior: reiterated the Q2FY27 target from the Q4FY26 call

call_points.text: Group same-store growth has slowed to 8-10% blended from a 25% post-COVID peak, with IT-ITES headcount a drag.
Tech revenue is only the core SaaS claims engine; AI features and outcome-based pricing are not yet billed.
Contract liability of ₹280.2 Cr is committed revenue not yet booked in the P&L.
On Bima Sugam, management said it expects no disruption to its business from the government marketplace.
The prior quarter's exceptional items and related insurance claims remain open and will be carried each quarter until concluded.
International business has no Middle East exposure; it operates in Continental Europe, Australia, New Zealand, Southeast Asia and the US.
No numeric FY27 revenue or margin guidance given; management frames FY26 as a milestone year.
50%+ of PHS claims volume migrated to MAtrix by Apr'26; Paramount to be primary engine by Q2FY27.
MAven Guard identified ~₹540 Cr of fraud, up 38.5% YoY.
Paramount's current negative margin profile is normalised in the steady-state PAT bridge, a management estimate.

operating_notes.text: FY26 exceptional items of ₹14.2 Cr comprised ₹3.77 Cr cyber-incident costs at Paramount TPA, ₹3.33 Cr new labour-code past service cost and a ₹7.10 Cr provision on advances to a customer.
Paramount TPA's TPA business was transferred to MAITPA by slump sale for nil consideration effective 1 February 2026, with deferred tax adjustments of ₹32.87 Cr.
₹49.60 Cr of the ₹198 Cr preferential issue was unutilised at 31 March 2026, held in four liquid funds of ₹12.50 Cr each and ₹0.05 Cr in the subsidiary's current account.
FY26: premiums administered (Group + Retail) ₹25,923.2 Cr, up 22.8% YoY; group market share 33.7% (+340 bps) and overall share 20.7% (+115 bps).
FY26: 100.3 lakh claims processed ex-SaaS; AI platform processes nearly one million claims a month; MAven Guard averted about ₹540 Cr of fraud.
FY26: more than 12,000 hospitals submitted claims monthly, with 14,000+ more accessible via Cashless Everywhere; Raksha Prime served 3.22 lakh patients across ~6,000 hospitals.
FY26: Group + Retail premiums administered ₹25,923.2 Cr (+22.8% YoY); overall market share 20.7% (+115 bps) and group market share 33.7% (+340 bps).
FY26: 10.0 million Group + Retail claims processed; 63% by volume cashless; end-to-end payment TAT improved to 7.41 days from 11.2 days.
FY26: Paramount to become the primary processing engine by Q2FY27; slump transfer to Medi Assist TPA effective Feb 1, 2026.
FY26: group premiums ₹23,000+ Cr (+25.6% YoY) with retention of 93.2%; retail TPA premiums ₹2,818 Cr (+4.2%) and retail TPA market share 5%.
FY26: MAven Guard prevented over ₹540 Cr of health insurance fraud; network discounts delivered over ₹1,300 Cr.
FY26: government business across 13 states and 3 union territories, with nearly a third of headcount contractually deployed serving 27 crore members through public health schemes.
Paramount corporate portfolio fully migrated; 100% of Paramount claims now run on MAtrix platform.
Managed premiums reached ₹24,752 Cr in H1FY27, including ₹9,648 Cr on the technology platform.
Fraud, waste, and abuse (FWA) savings reached ₹304 Cr in H1FY27, with 85% being AI-led.
H1FY27: group health benefits market share 34.1% (+182 bps YoY) with 90.5% client retention.
H1FY27: MAven Guard identified and stopped ₹304 Cr in fraud, waste and abuse.
H1FY27: three of seven contracted insurers fully live on the technology stack; four scheduled for H2FY27.

timeline.summary: Shareholders approved Ms. Sunita Rebecca Cherian (DIN: 10188170) as Non-Executive, Non-Independent Director via Postal Ballot on April 26, 2026, with 99.4555% voting in favor.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹241.99 Cr (+28.1% YoY), net profit to shareholders ₹53.44 Cr (+148.7% YoY).
Medi Assist filed its Reg. 32 statement for Q4FY26: ₹148.40 Cr of the ₹198 Cr October 2025 preferential issue utilised, ₹49.60 Cr unutilised, no deviation per CARE Ratings.
FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹904.8 Cr (+25.1% YoY), EBITDA ₹174.6 Cr (+13.3%), adjusted PAT ₹68.8 Cr, debt-free from January 2026 with ₹260.5 Cr free cash.

Medi Assist's Q4 & FY26 investor presentation (11 May 2026) reported FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹904.8 Cr (+25.1% YoY), EBITDA of ₹174.6 Cr at 19.3% margin, reported PAT of ₹89.3 Cr, and a debt-free balance sheet with ₹260.5 Cr free cash.
Medi Assist Healthcare Services Limited shared the audio recording of its earnings/conference call on May 11, 2026, discussing audited Q4 & FY2026 results via its website.

Medi Assist's Q4 & FY26 earnings call (11 May 2026) gave no numeric FY27 guidance, said tech and international growth should continue at FY26 rates, and put Paramount integration 1-2 quarters from completion.

On 20 May 2026, Medi Assist said the Regional Director, South Western Region, Bengaluru rejected the fast-track Section 233 application to merge International Healthcare Management Services Private Limited into Mayfair Consultancy Services India Private Limited and referred the scheme to NCLT, Bengaluru, citing no shareholder meeting and no consideration or swap ratio; the company said consolidated financials are unaffected.
Bessemer India Capital Holdings II Ltd. and its PAC declared no shares held in Medi Assist Healthcare Services Limited as of March 31, 2026, and ceased promoter status on April 2, 2026.
Q2FY27 results (consolidated): revenue ₹241.51 Cr (+3.9% YoY), net profit to shareholders ₹21.52 Cr (+170.7% YoY).
Medi Assist board approved a share buyback of up to ₹49.27 Cr at ₹425 per share via tender offer, with promoters abstaining.
Medi Assist filed the Q2FY27 monitoring agency report confirming zero deviation in the utilization of ₹198.00 Cr preferential issue proceeds.
Medi Assist reported Q2FY27 EBITDA margin recovery to 20.4% following the completion of Paramount integration and announced a ₹49.27 Cr share buyback.
Medi Assist reported H1FY27 operating revenue of ₹478.0 Cr (+13.0% YoY), EBITDA of ₹97.2 Cr (+19.0%) and margin of 20.3%, with SaaS revenue up 83.8% to ₹18.1 Cr.

status_history.evidence: Q4FY26 EBITDA margin reached 19.9%, but FY26 EBITDA grew 13.3% against revenue's 25.1%.
FY26 EBITDA margin 19.3%, down 201 bps YoY; Q4FY26 margin 19.9%, up 132 bps QoQ.

watchlist.response: Said it is very hard to forecast five years out; group yield changes partly reflect low-ticket benefits that are not fully priced, and internal effort-versus-life remuneration metrics are healthy or improving.
watchlist.text: Whether the TPA take rate can fall from 3.5% to 2.5% as IRDA pressures premiums and AI automates claims

watchlist.response: Declined to give a take-rate metric, saying the space is evolving; said tech margins could be 1.5-2x TPA but that this is not guidance.
watchlist.text: How tech revenue can be tracked against the ₹18,100 Cr of premiums on the platform

watchlist.response: Pointed to tech and international growth continuing at FY26 rates and the core business matching or bettering industry growth, without a numeric target.
